chunks: And from it, in the description of the sky:

He arranged the depressions and elevations of its openings without suspension, joined the widths of its breaches, and interwoven them with their counterparts. He made easy for the descending (angels) by His command, and for the ascending by the deeds of His creation, the steepness of its ascent. He called it when it was smoke, manifest, so the links of its joints joined together. Then He opened after the separation the silent doors, and set up a guard of shooting meteors upon its veil, and held it back from churning in the tearing of the air by His hands (power).
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the creation and structure of the sky in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from the 'Al-Ashbaah' chapter of Nahj al-Balagha poetically details the cosmic order, emphasizing Allah's command over the celestial spheres and the protection of the heavens from chaotic forces through the placement of meteors (shuhub). It reflects the Shia scholarly appreciation for the intersection of linguistic beauty and theological depth, illustrating how divine will maintains structural integrity in the universe. The description aligns with the Quranic narrative of the sky emerging from smoke, reinforcing the concept of a meticulously designed cosmos under constant divine supervision.
